name: Melanotan II
used_for: A synthetic cyclic peptide related to alpha-MSH that darkens skin and affects sexual function and appetite. It has no FDA-approved use and is sold online as an injectable or nasal tanning product. Published human studies are a handful of very small trials from the 1990s and 2000s (tanning, nausea and spontaneous erections in three men; erection studies in ten men each). A phase 2 vitiligo trial is registered in China but has no results.

entries.text: 0.01 mg/kg subcutaneous injections Monday to Friday for two weeks, escalated by 0.005 mg/kg to 0.025 or 0.03 mg/kg, in an alternating-day placebo design. The authors proposed 0.025 mg/kg/day for future phase I studies.
A single subcutaneous injection of 0.025 mg/kg versus placebo, with erections monitored for six hours.
entries.population: Ten men with psychogenic erectile dysfunction

entries.text: 0.025 mg/kg subcutaneously, given twice versus vehicle twice, in a crossover design.
entries.population: Ten men with erectile dysfunction with organic risk factors

internet_entries.text: A pharmacy and peptide retail site says melanotan II is commonly used at 0.25 to 0.5 mg subcutaneously daily in an initial phase and 0.5 to 1 mg one to two times per week afterward, with a stated maximum of 2 mg per day.
internet_entries.population: As described by the source, not a study population

internet_entries.text: A peptide guide site with affiliate links and discount codes says melanotan II is commonly used at 0.25 to 0.5 mg subcutaneously daily during an initial phase and 0.5 to 1 mg one to two times per week afterward.
internet_entries.population: As described by the source, not a study population

administration_guidance.text: A peptide information site that also sells or links to suppliers says Melanotan II is commonly injected at bedtime so that peak nausea falls during sleep, and that a mixed vial is kept refrigerated away from light for roughly 2 to 4 weeks. It also describes splitting a vial into single-use portions and freezing them to extend storage to a few months, while avoiding repeated freeze-thaw cycles.
administration_guidance.label: internet

administration_guidance.text: The Peptide Initiative, an educational site that does not appear to sell products, says evening or bedtime injection lets a user sleep through early nausea or flushing, that an empty stomach speeds absorption but may worsen nausea (a light snack 30 to 60 minutes beforehand is suggested), that food timing matters less after the first week, and that sites (abdomen, outer thigh, upper arm) are rotated to prevent fatty lumps. It also says a mixed vial is refrigerated at once and used within 28 to 30 days, with daily injections at first and fewer per week afterward.
administration_guidance.label: internet

administration_guidance.text: The same guide says brief UV exposure every few days during the early phase is needed to activate the pigment the body is producing. Melanotan II is unapproved and the sun exposure advice is a community claim, not an established practice.
administration_guidance.label: internet

side_effects.text: In small early trials in men, nausea was reported more often with Melanotan II than placebo, and 4 of 19 injections in one trial caused severe nausea.
side_effects.label: research

side_effects.text: Stretching, yawning and reduced appetite were reported more often with Melanotan II than placebo in ten men with psychogenic erectile dysfunction; none required treatment.
side_effects.label: research

side_effects.text: In a three-man pilot, spontaneous penile erections lasting 1 to 5 hours, mild nausea and, at the highest dose in one man, Grade II somnolence and fatigue were reported; two of three had increased skin pigmentation.
side_effects.label: research

side_effects.text: RxList, a medical reference website, lists nausea, stomach cramps, decreased appetite, flushing, tiredness, yawning, darkened skin and spontaneous erections as reported effects of Melanotan II.
side_effects.label: internet

side_effects.text: A peptide information site that also sells or links to suppliers says nausea and flushing are the most common early effects, along with reduced appetite, fatigue, yawning, mole darkening and new moles, and that many effects ease over the first one to two weeks of use.
side_effects.label: internet

internet_claims.claim: The Skin Cancer Foundation warns that Melanotan II is unapproved and unregulated, linked to serious risks including melanoma and muscle damage, and urges sunless tanners instead.
A dermatology practice says tan injections are unapproved, unregulated and risky (nausea, mole changes, sexual side effects, possible melanoma links), and recommends DHA self-tanners or spray tans.

The Peptide Catalog says Melanotan-2 darkens skin and raises sexual arousal through two receptor types and may suppress appetite, while advising a skin check; the site is an affiliate marketplace linking to suppliers and discount codes.
A clinic's blog says Melanotan II supports tanning, immune modulation, appetite control and sexual function, notes it is not FDA approved, and says it is offered only to the clinic's own patients.

research.summary: Pilot phase I study (Life Sci) in three healthy men given subcutaneous Melanotan II or saline on alternate days for two weeks.
research.finding: Two of three men had increased skin pigmentation. Side effects included nausea at most doses, stretching and yawning, spontaneous penile erections lasting 1-5 hours, and Grade II somnolence and fatigue in one man at 0.03 mg/kg. Three people is far too few to judge safety.

research.summary: Double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover study (J Urol) in ten men with psychogenic erectile dysfunction.
research.finding: Erections developed in 8 of 10 men after Melanotan II, versus little with placebo. Nausea, stretching and yawning and reduced appetite were more frequent than with placebo. Very small and short; it does not establish long-term safety.

research.summary: Double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover study (Urology) in ten men with erectile dysfunction and organic risk factors.
research.finding: Erections were reported after 12 of 19 Melanotan II injections versus 1 of 21 placebo doses, and sexual desire was higher. Nausea and yawning were more frequent, and 4 of 19 injections caused severe nausea.

research.summary: Registered phase 2, randomized, placebo-controlled trial (sponsor Hudson Biotech, site in Shenzhen, China) of Melanotan II added to narrowband UVB phototherapy in stable nonsegmental vitiligo; 60 participants planned; recruiting when checked.
research.finding: No results are posted, and the record does not state doses. It is registered in China, not in a US pipeline, so it does not make Melanotan II investigational in the US.

research.summary: FDA electronic reading room page (a 2016 notice of opportunity for hearing) that discusses an August 2007 FDA warning letter to a company marketing Melanotan II.
research.finding: The page says FDA treated Melanotan II as an unapproved new drug that could not be shipped across state lines without an approved application, and that the company had made unsubstantiated claims such as reducing skin cancer rates and curing rosacea.

research.summary: FDA web page on bulk drug substances nominated for compounding that may present significant safety risks (page dated 04/22/2026, fetched 2026-09-30).
research.finding: The page lists Melanotan II among substances nominated but withdrawn (not in the active Category 2 list), with this FDA statement: "Compounded drugs containing Melanotan II may pose risk for immunogenicity for certain routes of administration due to the potential for aggregation or peptide-related impurities. Published case reports discuss serious adverse events including melanoma, posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome, sympathomimetic toxidrome and priapism." The page does not make it an approved drug.

dose.summary: Not approved. Studied doses were about 0.01 to 0.03 mg per kg under the skin in three small trials of 3 to 10 men. Online sources describe fixed doses of 0.25 to 1 mg per injection, which have not been tested in that form.

mechanism.summary: Mimics alpha-melanocyte stimulating hormone (alpha-MSH) and switches on several melanocortin receptors. The tanning is thought to come from one receptor type and the sexual effects from another.

items.text: The molecule was described as having very strong melanotropic (pigment-stimulating) activity in the lab before the first human pilot.
items.label: research

items.text: Wikipedia says Melanotan II is a non-selective agonist of the melanocortin receptors MC1, MC3, MC4 and MC5, with tanning coming from MC1 and sexual effects from MC4 (and possibly MC3).
items.label: internet

items.text: A University of New South Wales (UNSW) news article says Melanotan II mimics natural hormones and raises the activity of pigment cells, causing tanning within days.
items.label: internet

best_documented_effect.summary: Small trials show it can cause erections and some skin darkening. There are only three tiny trials from the 1990s and 2000s, and the tanning data come from three men.

items.text: In ten men with psychogenic erectile dysfunction, 8 of 10 developed clinically apparent erections, with mean tip rigidity above 80% lasting 38.0 minutes on Melanotan II versus 3.0 on placebo (p=0.0045).
items.label: research

items.text: In ten men with organic erectile dysfunction, Melanotan II caused subjectively reported erections in 12 of 19 injections versus 1 of 21 placebo doses, and sexual desire was higher after Melanotan II.
items.label: research

items.text: In three healthy men, two had increased pigmentation of the face, upper body and buttock after five low doses over two weeks.
items.label: research

items.text: The Peptide Catalog, an affiliate marketplace that links to suppliers and discount codes, says it darkens skin, raises sexual arousal and may suppress appetite. The site advises a skin check.
items.label: internet

side_effect_groups.title: In trials
side_effect_groups.summary: In the small trials, nausea, yawning and stretching, less appetite and spontaneous erections were common. Most were mild, but 4 of 19 injections in one trial caused severe nausea.

items.text: In small early trials in men, nausea was reported more often with Melanotan II than placebo, and 4 of 19 injections in one trial caused severe nausea.
items.label: research

items.label: research

side_effect_groups.title: Online reports
side_effect_groups.summary: Websites list nausea, flushing, tiredness, less appetite, yawning, erections and darker or new moles. One seller says many effects ease in the first one to two weeks, which no trial tested.

items.text: RxList, a medical reference website, lists nausea, stomach cramps, decreased appetite, flushing, tiredness, yawning, darkened skin and spontaneous erections as reported effects of Melanotan II.
items.label: internet

items.text: A peptide information site that also sells or links to suppliers, says nausea and flushing are the most common early effects, along with reduced appetite, fatigue, yawning, mole darkening and new moles, and that many effects ease over the first one to two weeks of use.
items.label: internet

side_effect_groups.title: Serious reports
side_effect_groups.summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) cites published case reports of melanoma, brain swelling, sympathetic overstimulation and priapism (a painful, prolonged erection). Reviews say a link to melanoma is not proven.

items.text: FDA's page on compounding bulk substances says compounded Melanotan II may pose a risk of immune reactions from peptide clumping or impurities, and that published case reports describe serious adverse events including melanoma, posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome, sympathomimetic toxidrome and priapism.
items.label: research

items.text: Wikipedia says a 2013 review found no conclusive evidence that Melanotan II causes melanoma, a 2021 review said the increased risk can probably be explained by more UV exposure, and reported melanoma cases coincided with heavy sunbathing and sun bed use.
items.label: internet

items.text: A UNSW news article quotes a researcher saying case reports describe melanomas emerging from existing moles during or shortly after Melanotan II use, but evidence for a causal link is lacking.
items.label: internet

side_effect_groups.title: Regulator warning
side_effect_groups.summary: Regulators in the US, UK and Australia treat Melanotan II as an unapproved drug and warn against using it for tanning.

items.text: An FDA page discusses an August 2007 warning letter in which FDA treated Melanotan II as an unapproved new drug that could not be shipped across state lines and said the company made unsubstantiated claims such as reducing skin cancer rates and curing rosacea.
items.label: research

items.text: Nursing Times reported in 2008 that the UK medicines regulator (MHRA) called the product unlicensed, said it has not been tested for safety, quality or effectiveness, and told people not to use it.
items.label: internet

items.text: A UNSW news article says Australia's Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA) halted Melanotan II's development as a medicine for safety reasons and that advertising or supplying it to the public is illegal there.
items.label: internet
